description: Firefly AIO-3562JQ (Rockchip RK3562J) industrial board: the iCore-3562JQ module on the MB-Q-RK3562 carrier, the user's RK3562 module family. A board record: Atlas flashes it from maskrom (rockusb) with Rockchip's loader file and no vendor tool; running, it serves the identity contract (board-lite, gaia/device.toml), read-only. Written from Firefly's specification and wiki; untested on this board.

storage_target_evidence: Firefly iCore-3562JQ specification: storage eMMC, 16, 32 or 64 GB; no SPI flash listed.
Atlas writes the OS image to the eMMC from sector 0.
instructions: Connect its USB 3.0 OTG port to this computer.
Hold the MaskRom button, plug in the power (or press Reset), and release the button after about two seconds.
The board appears in maskrom (RK3562). Atlas checks the chip the loader reports, runs its DDR init and usbplug, writes the image to the eMMC, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: Sources: SoC, eMMC sizes, the USB 3.0/2.0 OTG port (shared with PCIe 2.1), the Recovery, MaskRom and Reset buttons, 12 V DC and two RJ45 are from Firefly's iCore-3562JQ_Specification.pdf (download.t-firefly.com, fetched 2026-11-02). The button sequence is Firefly's general one (hold the button, power on, release after one or two seconds): its 'Upgrade the firmware via USB cable' wiki page (wiki.t-firefly.com/en/iCore-3562JQ/03-upgrade_firmware.html) answered 404 here.

The maskrom PID 2207:350d is inferred, not read from a boot ROM: it is U-Boot's CONFIG_ROCKUSB_G_DNL_PID for RK3562 (rockchip-linux/u-boot next-dev 1c535d6, include/configs/rk3562_common.h:65), and that value equals the maskrom PID on every SoC checked (RK3399 330c, RK3566 350a, RK3588 350b, RK3528 350c, RK3576 350e). The earlier guess 350f is RK3506's (rk3506_common.h:55). No source names RK3562's maskrom PID, so the record stays pid_unconfirmed until lsusb on the board shows it; the chip the loader reports must read RK3562 before anything is written.

The loader file: rkbin 3e288fe's RKBOOT/RK3562MINIALL.ini builds rk3562_loader_v1.10.108.bin from rk3562_ddr_1332MHz_v1.10, rk3562_usbplug_v1.04 and rk3562_spl_v1.08 (all in fetch.lock; the merged file is Gaia's to build with boot_merger). Firefly's MiniLoaderAll.bin inside update.img is another file, which Atlas doesn't look for. No Gaia build for this board exists yet.
Whether the OTG port is a Type-A or Type-C connector on the carrier: the specification's drawing doesn't say.
Network: DHCP on the first RJ45 is assumed; which of the two (RGMII gigabit or RMII 100M) is eth0 is open.
